prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your needs. A few quick questions will let me give specific recommendations:
- Is this residential or commercial?
- Are you filing an insurance claim (storm/hail) or paying out of pocket?
- Do you have a ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas?
- Any preferences: asphalt shingles vs. metal vs. tile, brand certifications (GAF, Owens Corning), budget or timeline constraints?

While you answer, here’s a practical short guide so you can identify the best roofing company for your job.

What to look for in the “best” roofer
- Local experience in Dallas (storm/hail experience and local permit knowledge).  
- Proper insurance: general liability and workers’ comp — ask for certificates and call the carrier to verify.  
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.) — these improve warranty options.  
- Written estimates from at least three contractors that itemize materials, labor, tear-off vs. overlay, permit costs, cleanup, and disposal.  
- Clear warranty details: manufacturer (shingle) warranty and contractor workmanship warranty (ask how long and whether it’s transferable).  
- Positive, recent references and good reviews on multiple sites (Google, Yelp, BBB). Ask to see local jobs.  
- Permits and inspections: the contractor should obtain required City of Dallas permits and schedule inspections.  
- Reasonable payment schedule and lien releases: typical deposit is modest (often 10–30%), balance when work and cleanup are complete; insist on lien waivers.

Questions to ask any roofing company
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Dallas and do you pull the permits?  
- Can you provide proof of insurance and workers’ comp?  
- What manufacturer certifications do you hold?  
- What warranties come with the roof (manufacturer and workmanship)?  
- Will you provide references for recent Dallas-area roof replacements?  
- What is your expected start date and completion timeline?  
- How do you handle hidden damage (rot, decking replacement) and change orders?  
- What is the payment schedule and do you provide lien releases?

Red flags
- High-pressure sales tactics or an offer to waive your deductible.  
- Asking for full payment up front or insisting on cash-only.  
- No contract, vague scope, or reluctance to provide references/insurance proof.  
- Extremely low bid compared to other estimates.

Ballpark cost (very approximate)
- Full asphalt shingle roof replacement for a typical single-family home in Dallas can range widely depending on home size, pitch, and materials — often several thousand to tens of thousands of dollars. Get 3 bids and compare line items, not just total price.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code, roof type (asphalt shingle, metal, tile), and whether you’re using insurance. I’ll give 3–5 well-regarded Dallas-area roofers to consider and a prioritized checklist for choosing among their estimates.
